from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Putnam problems prioritize insight over computation.",
            "Shift your focus toward pattern recognition.",
            "Don't brute-force; look for elegant structures."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Putnam Mindset: Beyond Calculation", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the Putnam title at top center in #FFFFFF.
        self.title.set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fade in a 'Thinker' icon representing the mindset in #FFD700.
        thinker = Icon("fa-brain", color="#FFD700") # Using a placeholder icon or shape
        self.place_at_grid(thinker, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(thinker))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the text 'Beyond Calculation' in #FF4500.
        # Since 'Beyond Calculation' is part of the title, we modify the title color.
        # The prompt asks for highlighting 'Beyond Calculation'.
        # Let's use a rectangle highlight around 'Beyond Calculation' part of the title.
        
        # Adjust title to show it clearly
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(self.title, color="#FF4500", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(2)

class Icon(VMobject):
    def __init__(self, name, color=WHITE, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        # Using a simple circle to represent the brain/thinker for now
        self.add(Circle(radius=0.5, color=color, fill_opacity=0.5))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Toolkit: The Power of Invariants", [
            "Invariants remain constant despite dynamic change.",
            "Use invariants to track system state.",
            "Parity and coloring often reveal hidden answers."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        invariant_text = Text("Invariant", font_size=40, color="#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(invariant_text, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(invariant_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent shifting objects
        obj1 = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#ADFF2F", fill_opacity=0.5)
        obj2 = Square(side_length=0.7, color="#ADFF2F", fill_opacity=0.5)
        obj3 = RegularPolygon(n=3, radius=0.4, color="#ADFF2F", fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        objs = VGroup(obj1, obj2, obj3).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(objs, 'E3')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(objs))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))
        
        # Animation: shift positions while maintaining visual
        self.play(objs.animate.shift(UP * 1), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(objs.animate.shift(DOWN * 1), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash the invariant property
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(objs, color="#FF6347", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.play(Indicate(highlight, color="#FF6347"))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Strategic Heuristics: Extreme Principle & Descent", [
            "Consider the most extreme set elements.", 
            "Extreme points often force global constraints.", 
            "The extreme principle collapses search spaces."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'Extreme Principle' in #FF8C00
        text1 = Text("Extreme Principle", color="#FF8C00", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(text1, 'A2')
        self.play(Write(text1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a path descending to a minimum value in #7B68EE
        path = Arrow(start=self.grid['B2'], end=self.grid['E5'], color="#7B68EE")
        # Note: If custom pathing is needed beyond straight, use CurvedArrow or similar
        self.play(Create(path))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#7B68EE"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the minimal element in #FFFF00 for emphasis
        dot = Dot(self.grid['E5'], color="#FFFF00", radius=0.15)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot, scale=1.5))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF8C00"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Symmetry and Reduction", [
            "Identify symmetry to reduce problem complexity.",
            "Rotational symmetry simplifies complex systems.",
            "Map multi-variable systems to single representations."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        shape = RegularPolygon(n=6, color="#4682B4", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(shape, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(shape))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#4682B4"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#87CEFA"))
        self.play(Rotate(shape, angle=PI/3, run_time=2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF69B4"))
        
        # Representing reduction
        fold_shape = Polygon(ORIGIN, UP*1.5, RIGHT*0.75, color="#FF69B4", fill_opacity=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(fold_shape, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Transform(shape, fold_shape))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Putting it Together: The Final Proof Architecture", [
            "Structure your proof clearly and logically.",
            "Recognize hidden patterns to simplify integrals.",
            "Effective storytelling is key to proof architecture."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a structural map for a proof
        proof_map = VGroup(
            Square(color="#DCDCDC"),
            Line(UP, DOWN, color="#DCDCDC"),
            Circle(radius=0.3, color="#DCDCDC")
        )
        self.place_in_area(proof_map, 'A1', 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(proof_map))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#DCDCDC")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash connections between logic steps
        logic_conn = Arrow(self.grid['C3'], self.grid['D5'], color="#32CD32")
        self.play(Create(logic_conn))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#32CD32")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final result pops out prominently
        result_star = Star(color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(result_star, 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(result_star))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")

        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Putnam: Strategy and Intuition

sections.title: The Putnam Mindset: Beyond Calculation
sections.content: Transition from mechanical computation to 'Pattern Recognition'. Introduce the core philosophy: Putnam problems prioritize elegant, often non-obvious insights over brute-force algebra.
sections.example: A squirrel hiding nuts in a grid: Instead of calculating every spot, use the Pigeonhole Principle to prove at least one cache contains a specific density.

sections.title: Prerequisite Toolkit: The Power of Invariants
sections.content: Define 'Invariants'—properties that remain unchanged despite dynamic transformations. Use a visual graph showing a system evolving while a central 'knot' remains constant.
sections.example: A robot changing colors on a chessboard: If a move always flips adjacent squares, the parity of the colors remains invariant. We use this to solve complex tiling problems.

sections.title: Strategic Heuristics: Extreme Principle & Descent
sections.content: Introduce the 'Extreme Principle': If a set exists, consider the most extreme element (max/min). Visual: A mountain peak diagram where identifying the summit collapses the search space.
sections.example: Consider a set of points in the plane; look at the pair with the minimum distance. This 'local' extreme often forces a 'global' constraint that solves the problem instantly.

sections.title: Symmetry and Reduction
sections.content: Teach how to reduce complexity by identifying symmetries. Use visual overlays of rotational or reflective symmetry applied to complex geometric equations to simplify them.
sections.example: A spinning mechanical gear system: By assuming rotational symmetry, we can reduce a 10-variable system into a single representative variable equation.

sections.title: Putting it Together: The Final Proof Architecture
sections.content: Summarize the 'Look, Simplify, Solve' workflow. Emphasize that a clear logical narrative (the proof) is as important as the numerical result.
sections.example: Final walkthrough: A complex integral problem solved by recognizing a hidden symmetry (a secret mirror image in the function) that makes the area cancel out to zero.
